title: Iowa Army Ammunition Plant — emergency permit and supporting documents
summary: EPA public notice describing an emergency hazardous-waste storage and treatment permit for degraded lead azide. The page may be updated as legal and operational circumstances change; consult the source for current status.
notes: Primary source; not a claim about conditions at other facilities.

title: Emergency hazardous-waste permit for storage and treatment of lead azide (redacted PDF)
summary: Redacted EPA emergency permit for lead-azide storage and treatment; includes the agency's permit conditions and summary of alternatives discussed in supporting materials.
notes: EPA-issued source; permits and legal status may change.

title: Army article on alternative primary explosives and earlier Iowa stockpile concerns
summary: Army reporting states a research initiative began in 2004 in response to concerns about an approximately 40-year-old deteriorating lead-azide stockpile at this facility. The article does not establish that the specific inventory was identical to material discussed in 2026.
notes: Historical context only; no causal conclusion about subsequent decisions.

title: Toxic Fires — FOIA-derived investigation of military open burning and detonation (ProPublica)
location: Multiple U.S. military and contractor facilities
summary: ProPublica's interactive report on open burning and detonation sites draws in part on EPA hazardous-waste permit violation records obtained through FOIA for 1980–2017. Those violations concern site-wide hazardous-waste management, not necessarily the burn operations specifically.
notes: Independent journalism, not an agency FOIA release or evidence that a specific facility currently has unstable materials. Historical dataset.

title: Bombs in Your Backyard — FOIA-derived military cleanup database (ProPublica)
location: Current and former U.S. military sites
material: Environmental contamination and military munitions remnants
summary: Interactive database created using Defense Environmental Restoration Program records obtained through FOIA. The underlying government data were last updated in 2015 and describe historical cleanup and contamination sites, not current chemical stability assessments.
notes: See https://projects.propublica.org/bombs/methodology for source methodology and limitations. Historical cleanup sites should not be equated with unstable active stockpiles.

title: EPA fiscal year 2017 FOIA request log — prior military hazardous-waste inquiries
category: FOIA request log (not released responsive records)
material: Multiple subjects, including military hazardous-waste oversight
summary: EPA's archived fiscal-year 2017 request log documents prior inquiries, including ProPublica requests concerning Blue Grass Army Depot and Radford Army Ammunition Plant. A logged request does not establish that records were released or that reported concerns were substantiated.
notes: Examples: EPA-R4-2017-003466 (Blue Grass) and EPA-HQ-2017-010074 (Radford). Fiscal-year archive; exact document publication date not identified.

title: Iowa Army Ammunition Plant — environmental restoration administrative record
agency: Iowa Army Ammunition Plant / Army environmental restoration program
summary: Public administrative-record archive for CERCLA investigation and cleanup activities at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. Includes environmental studies, remedy-selection records, and an October 2026 record index. This is a restoration archive, not a confirmed inventory of currently unstable lead azide.
notes: Hosted through the installation's environmental restoration program. Documents have individual dates; the archive's October 2026 index is not a single publication date.

title: Army environmental assessment — lead azide risk mitigation at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant
summary: The Army's 2026 environmental assessment evaluates the proposed emergency disposal of degraded lead azide at Iowa Army Ammunition Plant and discusses alternatives and proposed mitigation measures. It analyzes a proposed action and does not establish the outcome of the operation.
notes: Document identified as IAAAP-EA-2026-01; posted by Army Sustainment Command on November 18, 2026. Separate from the emergency RCRA permit already indexed.

title: GAO-26-107065 — continuing resolutions and ammunition demilitarization delays
location: Selected U.S. Department of Defense activities, including Tooele Army Depot (Utah)
summary: GAO examined the effects of continuing resolutions on selected Department of Defense activities. Its Tooele Army Depot example documents that approximately 82% of ammunition rounds planned for demilitarization were processed in FY2024, illustrating backlog and funding constraints without establishing the delayed rounds were dangerously degraded.
notes: Published January 21, 2026; reissued with revisions February 4, 2026. Related to scheduling and funding, not a finding of imminent explosive instability.
